summary: Tongareva Airport (PYE/NCPY) serves Penrhyn Island, the northernmost and one of the most remote inhabited islands in the Cook Islands. Located in the Penrhyn atoll of the Northern Cook Islands, the airport provides a vital air link for the small local community primarily engaged in pearl farming and copra production. The remote location and surrounding turquoise lagoon make it a destination prized by adventure travelers and divers.
faqs:
Q: How do you get to Tongareva Airport?
A: Air Rarotonga operates scheduled flights from Rarotonga, with the journey taking roughly 3-4 hours depending on stops. Flights are limited, typically once or twice per week.

Q: Is there public transportation on Penrhyn Island?
A: There is no formal public transport system on Penrhyn. Most visitors arrange accommodation transfers in advance or hire local transport through their guesthouse.

Q: What facilities are available at the airport?
A: As a small island airport, facilities are minimal, typically including a small terminal building and basic check-in services. There are no ATMs or car rental counters on-site.

Q: Can you fly directly from Penrhyn to other Cook Islands?
A: Most flights connect through Rarotonga. Some itineraries may include stops at other Northern Cook Islands depending on the route.
transport_tips: Book flights well in advance as the limited schedule fills quickly, especially during the dry season (May to October). Arrange accommodation pickups before arrival since transport options on the island are very limited. Pack light as baggage allowances on small aircraft to remote islands can be restrictive.
local_tip: Bring cash in New Zealand dollars, as there are no ATMs on Penrhyn Island and card acceptance is limited even at small shops and guesthouses.
